report_name: 'Black October' Attacks Steal API Keys from Nine AI Dev Platforms

attack_patterns.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack_patterns.description: The primary objective of the Black October campaign was to steal API keys, a form of application access token, from environment variables on AI developer platforms.

attack_patterns.name: Resource Hijacking
attack_patterns.description: Attackers hijacked expensive AI model services using stolen API keys to run their own workloads, a technique dubbed 'LLMJacking', resulting in significant fraudulent charges for victims.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Attackers abused stolen API keys, which functioned as valid accounts, to make unauthorized calls to expensive AI model services.

attack_patterns.name: Cloud Instance Metadata API
attack_patterns.description: Attackers accessed and stole credentials stored in environment variables on cloud-based developer platforms, a technique analogous to querying cloud instance metadata services for secrets.

attack_patterns.name: Extract AI Model
attack_patterns.description: Attackers engaged in activity related to 'distillation,' a process of training smaller AI models by learning from a larger one, implying model extraction was performed using the stolen API keys.

attack_patterns.name: Deploy AI Agent
attack_patterns.description: Some victim platforms reported 'agent swarm' attacks, implying the use of multiple autonomous AI agents deployed by the attackers to carry out tasks using the compromised infrastructure.

campaigns.name: Black October
campaigns.description: A coordinated wave of attacks in October 2026 targeting at least nine AI developer platforms to steal API keys and other secrets from environment variables. The campaign utilized a technique dubbed 'LLMJacking' to hijack expensive AI model services for fraudulent use, leading to over $100,000 in fraudulent charges.

indicators.name: Anomalous AI API Usage
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous AI API Usage
id: 2b1c8e9f-4d5a-4b6c-8e7f-9a0b1c2d3e4f
status: experimental
description: Monitors for unusual usage patterns or sources for common AI API endpoints like /v1/chat/completions, which could indicate LLMJacking.
references:
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/black-october-for-ai-developer-platforms
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-01
tags:
  - attack.t1496
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri-stem|contains: '/v1/chat/completions'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate high-volume usage of AI services.
indicators.description: Detects unusual usage patterns or sources for common AI API endpoints, such as /v1/chat/completions, which could be an indicator of LLMJacking activity.

indicators.name: Anomalous Cloud Secret Enumeration
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Cloud Secret Enumeration
id: 8d7c6b5a-4f3e-4d2c-8b1a-0987654321fe
status: experimental
description: Detects anomalous enumeration or reading of environment variables or secrets manager services in cloud audit logs, a key tactic in the Black October campaign.
references:
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/black-october-for-ai-developer-platforms
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-01
tags:
  - attack.t1552.005
level: medium
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: auditlogs
detection:
  selection:
    OperationName|contains:
      - 'ListSecrets'
      - 'GetSecret'
      - 'ListKeyVaults'
  filter_known_principals:
    InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName|startswith:
      - 'legit-service-account@'
  condition: selection and not filter_known_principals
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative or deployment activities.
indicators.description: Detects anomalous enumeration or reading of environment variables or secrets manager services in cloud audit logs, which was a core tactic of the Black October attacks.

indicators.name: Suspicious Cloud Service Account Creation
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Cloud Service Account Creation
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a9b-8c7d-6e5f4a3b2c1d
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of new service accounts which may be used by attackers with stolen credentials to run workloads, as hinted in the Black October analysis.
references:
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/black-october-for-ai-developer-platforms
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-01
tags:
  - attack.t1078
level: low
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: auditlogs
detection:
  selection:
    OperationName: 'Create service principal'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate creation of new service principals for new applications or services.
indicators.description: Detects the creation of new service accounts, which attackers might use after stealing initial credentials to establish persistence or run their own workloads.
